page: Google Cloud Platform ct5lp-hightpu-1t is a specialized virtual machine within the ct5lp family, designed for hardware-accelerated workloads. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The primary hardware accelerator is a single Google TPU v5e with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM.

This server configuration does not include any local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage or cloud storage buckets. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external networking configurations for public internet access. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core represents a design tradeoff, prioritizing compute density and TPU acceleration over large system memory capacity.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ct5lp-hightpu-1t offers a highly targeted resource profile, minimizing system memory overhead to optimize the cost-to-performance ratio for TPU-driven tasks. This configuration is engineered specifically for machine learning workloads, including medium-scale deep learning model training, neural network inference, and data science pipelines that leverage Google TPU v5e hardware.
